title: Rav Sechorah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Nedarim 22b Rava praised Rav Sechorah to Rav Nachman as a great man, and Rav Nachman asked Rava to bring Rav Sechorah before him when he next came. It happened that he had a vow to annul; he came before Rav Nachman, who could not find grounds for dissolving the vow, and Rav Nachman was annoyed and said to him, “Go to your chamber.” Rav Sechorah went out and found an opening for himself: “Which is the straight path that a person should choose?” etc.

He was Rav Huna’s student, as Hyman says we always find “Rava said that Rav Sechorah said that Rav Huna said,” as in Berakhot 5a and 26a, Shabbat 24a, Eruvin 54a, Yevamot 106a, Bava Kamma 21a, Sanhedrin 49b and Menachot 40b.

In Bava Metzia 33a they disagreed about which teacher one must honor more than one’s father, and Rabbi Yose said: “Even if he enlightened his eyes only in one mishnah, he is his teacher.” Rava said of this: “Such as Rav Sechorah, who explained to me (the explanation of the mishnah of) zuhama listron [what it is].” Tosafot already treated this at length on Yevamot 106a and Avodah Zarah 19a. Seder HaDorot asks how Rava could say that he explained to him only this mishnah, when we find that he was his distinguished teacher, for he said several halakhot in his name. Hyman’s answer follows Tosafot on Sanhedrin 49b: everything Rava said in his name is only Rav Huna’s halakhot, and what he received from him himself is only the explanation of the mishnah; there is no need to elaborate further.
We find Rabbi Avina bar Sechorah, Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 10:5, and Rav Huna bar Sechorah, Chullin 107a.

notes.text: Saved Davidson Nedarim22b renders זיל לקילעך go to your tent, a dismissal; chamber is acceptable and sling is withdrawn. Preserve the return’s grounds for vow dissolution and the actual Avot-derived opening. The source’s teacher/pupil argument through Tosafot is Hyman’s; no silent conversion to a different Sechorah identity.

The consulted Tosafot Sanhedrin 49b first distinguishes what Sechorah taught on his own authority, then offers alternatives: even one teaching suffices, or Rava had not yet learned more at that time. Hyman selects the first explanation; the alternatives are not silently converted into his body. The dismissal in Nedarim 22b remains chamber/tent, with the withdrawn sling reading preserved historically.
